name: Macquarie Island
description: Macquarie Island is a narrow, windswept strip of land in the Southern Ocean, about 1,500 km south-east of Tasmania and roughly halfway to Antarctica. It is the only place on Earth where rock from the planet's mantle, normally buried some 6 km under the seafloor, is being pushed up above sea level. You can see it in the island's pillow basalts. In the nesting season, the whole royal penguin population gathers here.
